applicable_semantics.rule: when storage_kind = latch, the elements A5FF, B5FF, C5FF, D5FF are not storage elements: their ff_init and ff_srval relations are not applicable (not unknown); sr_kind is not applicable to a latch (its SR is asynchronous)
applicable_semantics.status: a model assumption drawn from docs/ff_latch_probe.md; a changed context is not an illegal configuration

meaning.driven: CE driven from the slice input

clock_mode.basis: the clkinv pair (fdce_inv: IS_C_INVERTED = 1 => bit 0 -> 1) for a flip-flop; the LDCE endpoint of docs/ff_latch_probe.md (CLKINV = 1 with IS_G_INVERTED = 0) for a latch; nothing attests a latch with the bit clear

meaning.inverted: IS_C_INVERTED = 1: the physical clock is the slice clock inverted
meaning.not_inverted: the physical clock (or gate) is the slice clock
meaning.unknown: no attested reading: the configuration is outside the model's domain

meaning.asynchronous: CLR / PRE, acting on the level
meaning.synchronous: R / S, acting at the edge

meaning.driven: SR driven from the slice input

meaning.latch: AFF..DFF are LDCE / LDPE; A5FF..D5FF are not storage elements

initialisation_event.allowed_context: the slice clock low and the SR input de-asserted (docs/b4_architecture.md section 5.1 step 2); an init step in any other context is refused by the model
initialisation_event.assumption: sets Q := INIT on every applicable element and clears nothing else; modelled on the UNISIM GSR

executing_side_visible: edge (rising | falling | null) of the slice clock
ce, sr, d (one bit per element, as applied)
q_before, q_after per element (0 | 1 | null = no readout given by the hypothesis for that element in that configuration, or never initialised)
host_only_diagnostics: the decode per element (primitive, INIT, SRVAL, CE / SR modes, kind, inversion)
the physical edge per element per step
observation_context.status: the executing side (the board, the cartographer, the search) sees only the first list; the second is derived from the decode and is for the host's audit and simulation reports, never an input to a decision in a session

primitive_selection.rule: by (storage_kind, sr_kind, SRVAL): flip-flop + synchronous + SRVAL 0 -> FDRE; + SRVAL 1 -> FDSE; flip-flop + asynchronous + SRVAL 0 -> FDCE; + SRVAL 1 -> FDPE; latch + SRVAL 0 -> LDCE; latch + SRVAL 1 -> LDPE (a latch's SR is always asynchronous; sr_kind is not applicable to a latch)

revision: 0.2.0 (2026-10-17, the owner's HOLD on 2bad829): the readings are machine enums validated by the loader (an unrecognised reading is refused, never read as a default); clock_mode is decoded BY STORAGE CONTEXT — under a latch the CLKINV bit is asserted with IS_G_INVERTED = 0 (docs/ff_latch_probe.md, 'The finding worth keeping'), so bit 1 means NOT inverted there and bit 0 has no attested reading (unknown: outside the model's domain); valid_configuration restated accordingly; the initialisation event's allowed context stated; the sources now include the latch probe record by path and digest.
scope: SLICE_X2Y25 (CLBLL_L_X2Y25, SLICEL_X0): the 21 addresses of the clb_ff_config class on that site, the eight storage elements of the slice. A model's definitions. Nothing here is a claim about silicon: no row below has been observed on a board (docs/b4_architecture.md section 4.4).

which address each of the 22 mine-site feature names moves (21 distinct addresses; CLKINV and NOCLKINV share one)
the specimen pair of every feature, from which the direction of every bit reading below is taken

items: the bit readings in `decode` (machine enums; the human meaning beside each)
clock_mode read by storage context: flip-flop — bit 1 inverted; latch — bit 1 NOT inverted (the attested LDCE endpoint), bit 0 unknown
the pin correspondence: the slice clock is C (or G for a latch), CE is CE (or GE), SR is R / S / CLR / PRE by the decoded kind and value

the initialisation event of the carrier is modelled as the UNISIM GSR, taken with the slice clock low and SR de-asserted: every applicable element takes its INIT — whether the carrier's event does so on silicon is condition A8 of docs/b4_architecture.md section 5.5

valid_configuration.rule: an assignment of the 21 bits is in the model's domain when every decoded reading is known; the one unknown reading is clock_mode bit 0 under storage_kind = latch, so those assignments are outside the domain and the model refuses to observe them by name
valid_configuration.status: a domain definition for the model (v0.2); not a statement that any configuration is legal to build, safe to write, or observed
